referenced_urls.title: How Do Small Coding Agents Use Code Graphs and Embeddings?

relevance: Tells local-model harness builders when code-graph tools are worth it.

media.description: Screenshot of a paper abstract testing whether embedding-search and code-graph tools help small open-weight coding agents on SWE-bench Verified, stratified by code-graph hop depth across Qwen3 and Gemma 4 sizes.
media.ocr_text: Coding agents are given embedding search and code-graph tools on the premise that a repository's structure is something the model lacks and the tool supplies. We test that premise on SWE-bench Verified with small open-weight models, stratifying tasks by a deterministic hop depth (the shortest code-graph path from code the issue mentions to code the gold patch changes) that a companion paper defines and validates. First, we ablate a localization agent's tool set (grep only; +embedding search; +graph tools; all) on a depth-balanced 160-task split and on all 500 tasks for ten models (six Qwen3 sizes from 0.6B to 32B with five decodings each, an FP8 control, three Gemma 4 sizes; 79k episodes). Structured tools double grep-only accuracy for Qwen3-8B and Gemma 4 E4B; their gain peaks at 17-21 points at 1.7-4B and falls to 4-5 points at 32B (odds ratio 0.77-0.82 per doubling of parameters).
